sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: This topic covers SOGA ss. 1–17 under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930. Read the statutory scheme as a coherent allocation of rights, duties, conditions, defences and consequences.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: SOGA ss. 1–17 must be broken into definitions, operative words, conditions, exceptions, savings and consequences. Map the agreement and commercial records to each statutory ingredient.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body:
1. Establish the transaction and parties.
2. Identify the statutory trigger in SOGA ss. 1–17.
3. Prove each constituent fact.
4. Test exceptions and defences.
5. Identify the precise legal consequence.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The asserting party ordinarily bears the initial burden on essential facts, subject to admissions and statutory presumptions. Electronic records should be authenticated and presented under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Check jurisdiction, limitation, arbitration or jurisdiction clauses, court fees and the exact relief. Verify the applicable Limitation Act Article and accrual date.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 1–3 establish the Sale of Goods Act and its relationship with the Indian Contract Act; sections 4–10 regulate sale and agreement to sell, formation, subject matter and price; sections 11–17 regulate conditions and warranties, title, description, quality or fitness and sale by sample.

Definition: This group establishes how a contract of sale is formed and the principal statutory conditions and warranties governing the goods.

Ingredients:
1. Identify buyer, seller, goods and price.
2. Distinguish a sale from an agreement to sell.
3. Establish a valid offer and acceptance for the sale.
4. Identify existing or future goods and price provisions.
5. Classify contractual stipulations as conditions or warranties and apply title, description, quality, fitness and sample rules.
examples: A sells a specific machine to B by description; if the delivered machine does not correspond with the contractual description, section 15’s statutory condition is engaged.
problemApplication: Apply sections 1–17: identify the statutory relationship or transaction, test each ingredient, consider exceptions or limitations, and conclude.
keyTakeaways: Sections 1–3 establish the Sale of Goods Act and its relationship with the Indian Contract Act; sections 4–10 regulate sale and agreement to sell, formation, subject matter and price; sections 11–17 regulate conditions and warranties, title, description, quality or fitness and sale by sample.
